about: What a search tool tells the agent about its `query` argument: the vendor language it reads, a grammar summary, two or three examples in that vendor's own syntax, and the free-text form where the real product has one. Served in the tool catalog (`query`) and appended to the MCP tool description. Every example is parsed and executed by tests/test_query_docs.py against the tool's connector definition, so a doc can never show a query the evaluator refuses.

jql.name: JQL (Jira Query Language)
jql.grammar: clauses `field OP value` joined by AND, OR, NOT and parentheses; OP is = != > >= < <= ~ !~ IN (..) NOT IN (..), IS EMPTY, IS NOT EMPTY; values are quoted strings, numbers, relative dates (-7d, -2w; units y M w d h m) or functions (now(), currentUser(), startOfDay(), startOfWeek(), startOfMonth(), endOfMonth(-1), ...); optional ORDER BY field [ASC|DESC]. Unknown fields are refused with Jira's own error.
jql.free_text: text ~ "words" searches every text field (summary, description, comments); summary ~ "word" searches one.
examples: project = OPS AND status = open ORDER BY created DESC
text ~ "vendor onboarding" AND labels IS NOT EMPTY

soql.name: SOQL (Salesforce Object Query Language)
soql.grammar: SELECT field, ... FROM Object [WHERE condition] [ORDER BY field [ASC|DESC] [NULLS FIRST|LAST]] [LIMIT n] [OFFSET n]; conditions use = != <> < <= > >= LIKE IN (..) NOT IN (..) INCLUDES EXCLUDES joined by AND, OR, NOT (parenthesise when mixing AND and OR); string values in single quotes; date literals TODAY, YESTERDAY, LAST_N_DAYS:n, THIS_QUARTER, ...; relationship paths such as Account.Name.
soql.free_text: SOQL has no free-text operator (that is SOSL). Use LIKE with % wildcards on a text field instead, for example Name LIKE '%renewal%'.
examples: SELECT Id, Name FROM Account ORDER BY LastModifiedDate DESC LIMIT 50
SELECT Id, Name, StageName, Amount FROM Opportunity WHERE StageName = 'Closed Won' AND CreatedDate = LAST_N_DAYS:90
SELECT Id, Name FROM Opportunity WHERE Name LIKE '%renewal%' LIMIT 20

encoded_query.name: ServiceNow encoded query (sysparm_query)
encoded_query.grammar: conditions `field<OP>value` joined by ^ (AND), ^OR (OR with the previous condition) and ^NQ (new OR'd query); OP is = != LIKE NOT LIKE STARTSWITH ENDSWITH IN (comma list) NOT IN ISEMPTY ISNOTEMPTY > >= < <= BETWEEN (a@b) ON; ORDERBYfield / ORDERBYDESCfield; dates as 2026-09-01 10:00:00 or javascript:gs.daysAgoStart(7) and the other gs helpers. As ServiceNow does, a condition on an unknown field is dropped rather than refused.
encoded_query.free_text: 123TEXTQUERY321=words searches the record's text (short description, description, notes).

odata.name: OData query options (Microsoft Graph)
odata.grammar: a bare $filter expression, or query options `$filter=...&$orderby=...&$top=n&$skip=n&$select=a,b&$search="terms"`; $filter uses eq ne gt ge lt le, in (..), and, or, not, parentheses, startswith(p,'x'), endswith(p,'x'), contains(p,'x'), p/any(v: v eq 'x'); strings in single quotes, dates as 2026-09-01 or 2026-09-01T10:00:00Z.

cql.name: CQL (Confluence Query Language)
cql.grammar: clauses `field OP value` joined by AND, OR, NOT and parentheses over space, type, title, text, label, creator, contributor, created, lastmodified, ancestor, parent, id; OP is = != > >= < <= ~ !~ IN (..) NOT IN (..); dates as "2026-09-01", now("-4w") or startOfMonth(); optional ORDER BY field [ASC|DESC].
cql.free_text: text ~ "words" searches page title and body; title ~ "word" searches titles only.
examples: type = page AND space = FIN AND lastmodified >= now("-4w") ORDER BY lastmodified DESC

kql.name: KQL (Keyword Query Language, Microsoft Search and SharePoint)
kql.grammar: free-text terms (all must match), "quoted phrases", prefix* wildcards, property restrictions prop:value (contains), prop=value, prop<>value and prop>date, prop>=date, prop<number; AND, OR, NOT in upper case, -term to exclude, parentheses. A restriction on a property the index does not know is searched as text, as SharePoint does.
kql.free_text: bare terms are the free-text form: budget forecast, or "budget forecast" for a phrase.

drive_q.name: Google Drive search query (q)
drive_q.grammar: clauses joined by and, or, not and parentheses: name contains|=|!= 'x', fullText contains 'x', mimeType = 'type', modifiedTime|createdTime > '2026-01-01T00:00:00' (RFC 3339), 'folderId' in parents, trashed = false, starred = true; each field accepts only the operators Drive documents for it.
drive_q.free_text: fullText contains 'words' searches file content and names; name contains 'word' searches names only.

slack_search.name: Slack search modifiers
slack_search.grammar: free-text terms (all must match), "quoted phrases", word* prefixes, -term exclusions; in:#channel, from:@user, before:/after:/on:/during: with YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM, today or yesterday; has:link, has:pin, is:thread. Repeated in: or from: are alternatives.
slack_search.free_text: bare terms are the free-text form: invoice approval.

predicate.name: structured predicate (no vendor query string)
predicate.grammar: this tool takes no query string. Pass `predicate` as {"entity": "<entity>", "where": [{"field": "<field>", "op": "eq|ne|gt|gte|lt|lte|in|contains", "value": <value>}]}; clauses are ANDed and `in` takes a list.
predicate.free_text: no free-text form: use op contains on a text field such as title or name.
